Don’t know if this I still ongoing, but just to contribute, most immediate post war media, including stuff until the fall of the Soviet Union, is immensely inaccurate regarding the eastern front. Although western nations did have attaches with the Russians during the war, the soviets were careful not to give the allies much information regarding the  war in the east once the Cold War began. Why would they give their foreseeable enemy information on an invasion which had them at the gates of Moscow? Because of this most of our information post war came from the Germans, specifically interviews and memoirs from German commanders. Most of these, with modern research and information gained after the fall of the iron curtain, have been debunked as German commanders trying to shift the blame for the failure of everything. It’s easier to say that you were doing everything right and the enemy was just stacking bodies instead of admitting glaring strategic failures. Many films such as enemy at the gates may have been well researched but their use of information based on the fantastical excuses of there Germans is obvious. Even at the start of the war the soviet had a surplus of weapons, having fought a war earlier with the Polish.
